items.title: South Korea withdrawing the ambassador from Ukraine is one of the most bizarre moves I have seen in some time. Seoul even says that it received a letter from the Ukrainian foreign ministry which included an apology, but apparently it wasn’t enough. Ukraine is literally fighting South Korea’s primary enemy and the government in Seoul has nothing better to do than to yearn for an „extraordinary“ apology. Something very fishy is going on here and it has nothing to do with the North Korean soldier which Ukraine captured. The fact that it has been recently revealed that South Korean oil deliveries ended up in Russia is only one explanation. But I’m gonna be honest, not even that explains sufficiently the extreme lengths they are going.

🇺🇦Ukrainian Groupings and Corps sectors - a basic guide
This thread is an introduction to 🇺🇦Ukrainian “Force Groupings” and Corps deployments as of late summer 2026.
We have noticed several misconceptions on the topic, shared by analysts and the “broader public” alike.
Our information is exclusively based on open sources and observation of publicly available data.
❗️Before we begin, a fundamental notion must be clear: at the moment, the corps headquarters and their organic brigades should be treated separately.
With a few exceptions, most corps do not have all their brigades in their assigned sector (and many brigades are subordinated to corps they do not organically belong to).

items.title: RT by @DefMon3: "The first word brigade and corps commanders use to describe the first few months of Drapatyi's tenure is 'freedom'. Unlike his predecessor, who would tell some brigade commanders how and where to fight – even specifying the coordinates where a position should be set up – Drapatyi has chosen a different approach. He has opted to decentralize command, moving away from the 'micromanagement' that has already become widely known to the public... Ukrainska Pravda sources say the move away from hands-on management of brigades and corps has brought another change: Drapatyi no longer spends several hours every day hearing reports from all commanders, as Syrskyi did. 'Syrskyi would hear reports from everyone every day and could give specific instructions on how to respond to developments, including where troops should advance… Drapatyi doesn't do that; that's the job of the troop grouping commanders. Drapatyi focuses on strategic and systemic issues. And when commanders do speak to the commander-in-chief, he isn't interested in a standard report on 'what happened', but in statistics, analysing problems and finding solutions – in other words, what conditions need to be created for a particular commander to accomplish their mission. And that's the right approach,' a senior military officer told Ukrainska Pravda." https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/10/05/8056518/

Драпатий цього не робить, це робота угруповання військ Драпатий зосереджується на стратегічних і системних питаннях.
